chunks: 1769 - It is narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام that he said:

"A group of Jews came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and the most learned among them asked him about certain matters. Among what he asked him was that he said to him: 'For what reason did Allah, Mighty and Majestic, make sawm (fasting) obligatory upon your Ummah in the daytime for thirty days, while Allah made it obligatory upon the nations more than that?' So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: 'Indeed, when Adam عليه السلام ate from the tree, it remained in his belly for thirty days. So Allah imposed upon his progeny thirty days of hunger and thirst, and what they eat at night is a grace from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon them. And thus it was for Adam عليه السلام. So Allah imposed that upon my Ummah.' Then he recited this verse:
"Prescribed for you is fasting as it was prescribed for those before you, so that you may attain taqwa. [For] numbered days."

The Jew said: 'You have spoken the truth, O Muḥammad.' Then, 'What is the reward of one who fasts them?' So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: 'There is no believer who fasts the Month of Ramaḍān seeking reward except that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, makes obligatory for him seven qualities. The first of them is that the haram in his body melts away. The second is that he draws near to the mercy of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. The third is that he will have expiated the sin of Adam, his father, عليه السلام. The fourth is that Allah makes easy for him the agonies of death. The fifth is security from hunger and thirst on the Day of Resurrection. The sixth is that Allah gives him acquittal from the Fire. And the seventh is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, feeds him from the wholesome things of Paradise.'
He said: 'You have spoken the truth, O Muḥammad.'"

key_terms.بَرَاءَةً مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ: acquittal and safety from the Fire
key_terms.تَتَّقُونَ: that you may attain taqwa, God-consciousness and piety
key_terms.تَفَضُّلٌ: a gracious favor or bounty from Allah
key_terms.ذُرِّيَّتِهِ: his progeny, referring to the descendants of Adam عليه السلام
key_terms.سَكَرَاتِ ٱلْمَوْتِ: the agonies or throes of death
key_terms.ٱلصَّوْمَ: sawm (fasting), the prescribed abstention during the daytime
key_terms.ٱلصِّيَامُ: fasting, as mentioned in the Qur'anic verse

ai.seo_question: Why did Allah prescribe thirty days of fasting in Ramaḍān for the Ummah of Prophet Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and what reward does the fasting person receive?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the obligation of the thirty-day fast of Ramaḍān by linking it to the account of Adam عليه السلام and then cites the Qur'anic basis for fasting. It also describes seven spiritual and eschatological rewards for the believer who fasts Ramaḍān with sincere intention and in hope of divine reward.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1769 - It is narrated from Imam al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) that he said:
"A group of Jews came to the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings be upon him and his family), and the most learned among them asked him about certain matters. Among the questions he asked was: 'Why did Allah (swt), the Almighty, prescribe fasting during the day for your community for thirty days, while He prescribed fasting for more than that for other nations?'
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'When Adam (as) ate from the tree, the effect of it remained in his stomach for thirty days. Therefore, Allah (swt), the Almighty, prescribed for his progeny thirty days of hunger and thirst. And what they eat at night is a favor from Allah (swt), the Almighty, upon them. The same was the case with Adam (as). Thus, Allah (swt) prescribed it for my Ummah.'
Then he recited this verse: "Fasting is prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you, that you may attain taqwa. [It is for] a fixed number of days." (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:183)
The Jewish man said: 'You have spoken the truth, O Muhammad (sw). What is the reward for one who fasts them?'
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) replied: 'No believer fasts the Month of Ramadan sincerely, seeking its reward, except that Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, grants him seven virtues:
1.	The first is that the forbidden (haram) in his body melts away.
2.	He will draw closer to the mercy of Allah (swt), the Almighty.
3.	He will have atoned for the sin of his father, Adam (as).
4.	Allah (swt) will ease for him the throes of death.
5.	He will have security from hunger and thirst on the Day of Resurrection.
6.	Allah (swt) will grant him immunity from the Fire.
7.	Allah (swt), the Almighty, will feed him from the pure delights of Paradise.'
The Jewish man said: 'You have spoken the truth, O Muhammad (sw).'"
